{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.5 (Commerce One / Corio Agreement)

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel 
**Re:** Playbook review of the licence and hosting agreement — we act for Corio (Customer/Licensee)

---

## Executive summary

We have reviewed the Agreement against the playbook. Nineteen rules were assessed: ten clauses are compliant (several at the fallback rather than the preferred position), six are deviations requiring redlines, and two rules are unaddressed in the document.

The commercial architecture is broadly acceptable and, in several respects, favourable to us: the Section 8 IP indemnity runs one way in our favour and is expressly carved out of the liability cap and the consequential-damages exclusion, so it is uncapped — better than our fallback. There is no exclusivity, non-compete, MFN, minimum-volume commitment, non-solicit or Customer-payable liquidated damages anywhere in the Agreement, and the Section 4.4 audit right already meets our preferred position on frequency, notice, auditor independence and cost allocation.

Our concerns are concentrated in three places. First, the Section 13.5 carve-out transfers ownership of Corio-created Developments to Commerce One wherever Commerce One supports them on an ongoing basis, with no licence back — an effective transfer of our own hosting-integration IP, which the playbook treats as walk-away territory. Second, Section 9 caps liability at amounts actually paid "for the transaction which the liability relates to" and carves out only Section 8, omitting confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct. Third, we are committed to a five-year initial term with no convenience exit, no post-termination transition assistance or data-return right, and no vendor insurance covenant. The Section 7.3 warranty (60 days from the Effective Date, sunsetting 31 December 1999) can expire on or before acceptance, leaving effectively no post-acceptance coverage.

---

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant (exceeds fallback; uncapped) | § 8 Indemnification |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Deviation** | § 13 Shared Resources (13.5) |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | **Deviation** | § 9 Limitation of Liability |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant (preferred) | Sales and Marketing Cooperation (Exhibit D) |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Compliant (preferred) | § 11 Term and Termination |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | § 2 Grant of Rights |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant (preferred) | § 2 Grant of Rights |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Deviation** | § 11 Term and Termination |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant (preferred) | § 4 Fees (4.4) |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant (at fallback) | § 14 Miscellaneous (14.3) |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | Compliant (preferred) | § 4 Fees |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase / volume commitments | Compliant (preferred) | Pricing (Exhibit B) |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant (preferred) | § 14 Miscellaneous |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice | Compliant (preferred) | § 11 Term and Termination (11.1) |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | **Missing** | § 11 Term and Termination |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Deviation** | § 7 Warranties and Disclaimer (7.3) |
| Low | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | **Deviation** | § 14 Miscellaneous (14.1) |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | § 14 Miscellaneous |

---

## Walk-away items

These three points are identified in our review as falling into walk-away territory and should be resolved before signature:

1. **Ownership of Corio-created Developments (§ 13.5).** The carve-out awarding Commerce One "all ownership rights, including intellectual property rights in the Developments" where it supports them on an ongoing basis, with no licence back to Corio, is walk-away territory and fails the fallback because we retain no perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free right to use or modify code we created and paid for. Our redline deletes only the carve-out; Commerce One's pre-existing materials and the Software are untouched.
2. **No customer termination for convenience in a five-year term (§ 11).** The only exits are non-renewal at expiry and termination for material breach or insolvency. Absence of any convenience right during a multi-year commitment is walk-away territory. We propose a 30-day convenience right with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees and no penalty (preferred position); 60 days' notice is available as a fallback.
3. **No vendor insurance (§ 14).** The Agreement contains no insurance clause at all, and Commerce One hosts the MarketSite Service and handles Corio and Customer data. We have inserted a new Section 14.10 at the preferred position (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, workers' compensation, certificates on request), with the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) offered in the comment.

---

## Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the six deviations and two missing clauses:
   - § 13.5 — delete the ongoing-support ownership carve-out.
   - § 9 — mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and US$1,000,000; add an Excluded Claims definition (indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement); confirm Corio's fee obligations are not capped damages.
   - § 2 — add an Affiliate definition and extend the 2.1 and 2.2 grants to our Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf ("Affiliate" currently appears nowhere in the Agreement).
   - § 11 — new convenience-termination right (30 days, pro-rata refund) and new § 11.4 (up to six months' transition assistance at then-current rates; data return in a commonly used machine-readable format within 30 days of request; deletion with written certification), carved back for Commerce One's surviving obligations and legal retention so it does not cut across the § 11.3 run-off.
   - § 7.3 — Product Warranty Period of twelve months from acceptance (fallback: 90 days from acceptance), replacing 60 days from the Effective Date with the 31 December 1999 sunset.
   - § 14.1 — add a "not unreasonably withheld" standard and an affiliate carve-out.
   - New § 14.10 — vendor insurance covenant.
2. **Sequence the negotiation** around the three walk-away items first (§ 13.5 ownership, § 11 convenience exit, insurance), then the § 9 cap, then warranty duration, licence scope and assignment.
3. **Hold in reserve** as drafting points only if the counterparty reopens the relevant clause: an express Customer Data / hosted data ownership statement and the deferred question of ownership of Software enhancements (§ 13.5 final sentence); a quantified audit notice period and auditor confidentiality undertaking (§ 4.4); a 60-day renewal reminder and a renewal price-uplift cap (§ 11.1); and Commerce One's 30-day (rather than 90-day) non-renewal notice.
4. **Flag to the engrossing team** the duplicated/garbled text in Section 9 (p0092) for deletion as a scrivener's error, and note that the disclaimer text at p0084 is truncated in our copy — we should confirm against a clean execution version that it reaches only implied warranties.
5. **Do not spend capital** on the noted sub-element gaps in the indemnity (no cover for breach of law, unauthorised data disclosure or gross negligence/wilful misconduct; refund tied to fees "paid" rather than "paid or payable"), given the uncapped IP indemnity and the absence of any reciprocal indemnity from us; nor on § 14.3, which sits at the accepted fallback (California law, San Francisco venue, domestic AAA seat).
"}
